minimum_consumer_change.search: Add the five exact heading units to live book-local search and export the same units into the regenerated cross-page index. Retain the current paragraph units and all 17 new atlas claim entries.
minimum_consumer_change.same_page_constraint: An edit to generated reader-index.js alone is insufficient: reader.js remoteUnits() excludes same-page units. The book-local unit construction must expose the heading units as well.
minimum_consumer_change.links: Preserve the eight exact labels as actual links to their existing index.html# or atlas.html# targets. This needs only the existing same-bundle routes; it does not require external-link support.
minimum_consumer_change.authored_content: Derive titles, labels and destinations verbatim from the pinned source values above. No prose, formula, heading, ID or status rewrite is authorized by this receipt.
minimum_consumer_change.presentation: Use the existing search result and link presentation. No new layout, CSS, interaction architecture or visual design is specified.
minimum_consumer_change.ownership: Root authorizes and records the separate consumer patch; the build/code owner implements and verifies it. This author has changed no source, renderer or built output.

bounded_acceptance_after_repair: All five exact page/id/title tuples occur once in the live book search export and regenerated cross-page index.
A search for each exact authored title offers a result reaching its existing heading anchor on the appropriate page.
The eight exact visible labels are actual hyperlinks with the authored same-bundle hrefs, and each target exists once.
The existing paragraph coverage, all 17 new atlas search entries, visible supplement words/formulas and the closed scientific source outputs remain unchanged.

The consumer patch and regenerated outputs are recorded by the build owner; original candidate failures remain preserved as historical evidence. Opus rendered verification and publication remain separate.
